They're both terms that were originally developed to refer to the more obnoxious members of a fanbase, but then got adopted and owned by less obnoxious members until the insulting connotations largely died out. Older fans may still use them in the original sense, but that meaning is increasingly lost on younger ones.

Like personally, I would generally use 'otaku' for fans laser focused on specific subgenres who don't care about any other genres and don't really distinguish good or bad within their subgenre. And I'd use weeb to refer to anime fans who are relatively new to the hobby, only watch the most popular stuff, and are likely prone to peppering their speech with the ten Japanese words they know.

But both of those definitions have been lost to time...

I started in college twenty years ago, took three years there, the third in a study abroad program with a dedicated Japanese curriculum, then spent another three or four years living in Japan self-studying while immersed in the culture and reading a ton of manga and novels and watching a ton of anime and live action stuff with no subtitles.

I eventually got the top level Japanese Proficiency exam and started working as a professional translator, which I've now done for over a decade. I've played all four Japanese-only Trails games in Japanese and was thankful I have the ability to do so--but they're HARD. Even at my level they're throwing vocab at me I don't know. Up there with Tanya the Evil or Twelve Kingdoms on the 'god damn it I have to go look up something again' (or just guess from context) front.

Learning Japanese is totally worth it, but some less lofty goals will help you avoid getting discouraged along the way.
